title: A Peek into Fate
subtitle: Even the untouchable has a texture.

items.text: A Peek into Fate

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Then the attack on the SPDM was a diversion. They wanted to pull Foundation forces away from headquarters.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Right now, Arcana has found her way into the Foundation, and the "Storm" is closing in on SPDM.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: And here we are stuck in whatever this place is, doing nothing.
Her low muttering makes the corridor feel all the more desolate.
Brushed by a fingertip, the golden threads begin to drift through the air. Their knotted forms tremble in the darkness.
Somewhere within the body, an innate ability, mysterious and distant, is quietly waking.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think I've found a path. Let me try something.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, this way. This is our way out.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But you're pointing out the window.
Her mind tries in vain to make sense of what her eyes are taking in.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then we need to jump out of it. Just trust me.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Of course.
She opens the window. Below them lies the garden that the Foundation so carefully tends to its trademark austere perfection.
Conviction and trust conquer her innate fear of heights.
She climbs onto the windowsill first and crouches there, then offers her hand.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Please take my hand. Slowly, please. Careful.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's get out of here.
The labyrinth created by the "boon" is silent and void of any traces of life.
But in free fall, the wind's howl still passes through the ears.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto!
At some point, the tightly clasped hands loosen as the two plunge into darkness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mmm?
The fall has stopped. The body is upright, feet pointed down, no longer adrift in the void.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: My sight's restored. I can see again.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, wait.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: These threads, the woven net ... I've seen this before.
The golden threads drift against the fingertips, like the strings of an instrument waiting to be played.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What are they? I can touch them, even pluck them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why are they revealing themselves to me?
"You know the ways of time and fate."
The palm presses onto the sand table, which is nearly submerged in the black torrent.
The black tide recedes, and in its wake, it leaves an unstable seed.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is this another game of yours, Arcana?
The tower of threads, gnawed full of holes, sways as if built on shifting sands.
Right before it crumbles, the hand instinctively reaches out  and catches this precarious destiny.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: One day, I will uncover its secret.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: The door's open, again.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: The thing we're after should be right behind it.
Merel presses a hand to the somehow unlocked door and pushes it open a crack to peer inside.
Merel pushes the children back before slipping inside.
She pulls the door shut.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Stay back. Don't come in.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: What? What's wrong? What's in there?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: It's ... It's better if you don't see.
She turns around and locks the door, locking the children away from the sight that now confronts her.
At last, an explanation for the missing teachers and guards. Dreadful as it may be.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: All the instructors, the guards, even the principal ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Ugh!
She forces back the bile rising in her throat at the sight.
Yet despite the carnage, she feels almost calm.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Alright, Merel. You can't mess this up.
The SPDM's last line of defense against the "Storm" has fallen from its perch. The Dove's body, split into two, lies bloodstained and battered on the floor.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Shelter Dove's gone. But there should still be spares somewhere.
She kneels and pushes a corpse aside, searching for an intact Shelter Dove.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Come on, now. They're only dead people. They can't hurt you.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: You've seen worse. With Charon, remember? I wonder what he'd do if he were here.
She blinks. With mechanical movements, she turns over another instructor's lifeless body.
Sheltered beneath the body lie several Shelter Doves, mercifully undamaged.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Ms. Fogel ...
Memories of her flood through Merel's mind, but one thing she refuses to do is think on the anger she once felt at her for sending her to detention all those years ago.
She wipes away the tears welling in her eyes with a shaky hand, then gathers the Shelter Doves in her arms.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Merel? Are you okay in there? It's getting dark outside.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Y-Yes. I found it. Just a minute. Stay right there.
The solemn shutting of the door behind her feels like shoveling the last bit of dirt over a grave.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: So, inside there ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Your teachers and the guards did everything they could to protect you. That's all you need to know.
The students can read the overwhelming sorrow on her face, but they remain silent, unsure of what to say.
The clouds heralding the "Storm's" arrival have blotted out the sun, and the loss of power has plunged the school into darkness. The Doves she holds are their only source of light.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Take these.
She hands the Shelter Doves to the students, keeping one tucked into her own arms.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Glowing doves?

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: You came all this way for some dove sculptures?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Yep. Now, we need to get these to the library. They're our only chance to survive the "Storm."
She's given up on concealing the "Storm" from them, protocol or not.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: But what about the monsters? They could still be on the first floor.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Leave them to me. I'll get you out safely.
Merel leads them back to the second floor. The blast door leading to the first floor is just as they'd left it—locked.
She presses an ear to the door and frowns when she hears footsteps behind it.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Listen carefully. You two hide in the air vent.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll go first and draw the monsters upstairs. You go down the vent to the ground floor and run as fast as you can to the library.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: But what about the monsters outside? How-How can Emilia and I get past them?
Lucas's bravado disappears and the terrified child remains.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: I know exactly what to do.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: We use your invisibility grenade before we get out of the vent. Then we just have to get to the library before it wears off.
Emilia details her plan with confidence.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Brilliant, Emilia. You do exactly that. Take the Dove to the library to save your friends. Assistant Monitor Lavender will be there. I'm sure she'll be impressed.
A powerful burst of arcane energy blasts a hole through the door.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: No. That glow ... I've seen it before.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So, there's more than one of those things.
Another beam cuts through the hole, this time striking the wall just above the vent.
Rubble falls and blocks the vent's entrance, but the impact also blasts a hole in the watchtower's wall.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Emilia? Lucas? Are you alright?

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: I'm fine. We're fine.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: It-It tore a hole through the wall, just like that.
A familiar, intact head peeks through the hole in the door.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Bloody!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Move, now. Through the opening. I'll help you land with a levitation incantation.

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: What about you?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll be right behind you. Remember, once you land, run straight to the library. Watch out.
The door, unable to withstand further damage, falls to the ground.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Go! Now!
Merel hoists them up and pushes them through the hole.

items.speaker: Emilia & Lucas
items.text: Ah!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Ŝvebi   Stay!

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Merel!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll see you at the library.
She turns and dodges as an energy beam carves through the wall behind her and continues into the "Storm"-wrecked sky.
The disciple lowers its hand and approaches the opening in the wall, intent on breaking through it.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Not so fast. You'll have to get through me first.
The disciple's head sways as if pondering a choice. Finally, it turns to face its enemy.
Merel loads her last clip and takes a deep breath.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I've killed your kind before. I know just where to aim.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Even if I'm on my own this time—

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'm more than enough to take you down!
Soft tissue flows from its cracked skull.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: That's for breaking my Dove. Ugh!
A sharp pain shoots up her leg.
Merel lowers her gun and looks to the Shelter Dove in the corner—damaged mid-combat.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Could be worse. Just need to remember what Marsha showed me.
She slumps down against the wall, tears off part of her coat, and begins bandaging her wound.
The pain spikes again as she tightens the cloth around it.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Imagine her face. Urgh, if she could see me now. Tch!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Not just Marsha, all of them—Charon, the "XII," Vertin ... I'll tell them—urgh! That should do it.
With the wound now dressed, she lifts herself to her feet. She can walk, but each step comes with a wave of pain.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll tell them I didn't run away this time.
She finds herself at the watchtower's base and leans onto its doorframe. The world outside looks as though it's burning.
Rainwater gathers to form a puddle in a nearby crater.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: That must've been Emilia's grenade. I knew you could do it, kid.
The raindrops begin to rise.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: The "Storm" ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I've got to get back to the library. I have a promise to keep.
She casts aside her now-useless pistol and everything else weighing her down. All that's left in her arms is the dimming Shelter Dove.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I really hope there won't be any more battles after this.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Now, come on. After everything I've been through ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I can survive this!
She rushes into the rain.
